items.title: Department of Rural Development and DAHD Join Hands to Boost Fodder Production, Strengthen Livestock Infrastructure and Support Rural Livelihoods under VB–G RAM G
items.summary: The initiative adopts a whole-of-government approach to address fodder scarcity, strengthen livestock-related infrastructure and support the livelihoods of rural households, particularly small and marginal farmers and landless families dependent on livestock and dairy activities.

facts.text: The VB–G RAM G Act, which came into force on 1 July 2026, provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment per rural household and focuses on the creation of durable assets across four thematic areas, including livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events.
These cover interventions relating to fodder cultivation and storage, pasture development, livestock shelters, dairy infrastructure and veterinary health facilities.
Construction, repair and maintenance of livestock shelters for eligible beneficiaries and communities, including cattle, goat, piggery and poultry shelters, as specified in the approved list.

The advisory calls upon States and Union Territories to prepare comprehensive State Action Plans for fodder security and livestock infrastructure through convergence among the Departments of Rural Development, Animal Husbandry, Agriculture and other relevant sectors.

facts.text: Since Mandatory gold hallmarking was introduced in 2021, over 65 crore gold articles have received Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) numbers as of 15 October 2026.

The Hallmarking Scheme for silver articles was launched in 2005 .
